items.message: This change implements GATE-REVIEW-8: a second `/implement` on a ticket with an open change request updates that request rather than opening a duplicate. The diff spans both host adapters (GitHub and GitLab), the `implement_propose` orchestration, a new `update_reviewable` helper, `fetch_branch` on `GitLocal`, and a full test file. The description is detailed and the implementation matches it at every point I could verify. The design choices are argued in the code and the gate entry — the lease …[truncated]
`assert_run_scoped` is called on a branch opened by a different run — it may refuse legitimately.
`_existing_change_for` swallows `changes_for` errors silently and falls through to open a new PR, but logs nothing.
The real-git tests use `file://` remotes, which do not exercise the token-in-URL credential shape the refusal comment argues about.

This change adds the update-existing-change-request path for a second `/implement` on a ticket that already has an open pull request. From a performance angle, the new `_existing_change_for` and `_branch_state` helpers each do a bounded number of operations: one `changes_for` API call, one `fetch_branch` (a single git fetch + rev-parse), and one `commits_between` over the range `HEAD..<sha>`. None of these scale with anything unbounded in the steady state — a ticket's open change requests are a …[truncated]

This change adds the update-existing-change-request path for a second `/implement` run: it force-pushes to the prior branch with a lease on the sha read at inspection time, refuses branches carrying person-commits or unreadable branches, and marks the change request back to draft when tests are red. The security-relevant properties I weighed are: credential leakage in `TargetRefused` prose, the TOCTOU window between the branch read and the push, and the trust boundary on branch content before ov…[truncated]
git stderr printed to stdout before being suppressed from the public refusal — if stdout is captured and forwarded, the credential reaches the same surface.
Same stdout print of git stderr in the GitLab adapter — same narrow credential-reach concern.

This change introduces GATE-REVIEW-8: a second `/implement` on a ticket with an open change request force-pushes to that branch rather than opening a second pull request. The test coverage is extensive and unusually self-aware — several tests exist explicitly to prevent the class of assertion error the first version of this very file contained (comparing two constants, `hasattr` on the wrong object). I checked every named behaviour in the gate text against the tests: the update path, the person-…[truncated]
test_two_open_crs_uses_the_one_resolved_through does not assert which URL appears in the comment when only one CR exists.
_Local.commits_between ignores its arguments, so tests that pass a specific `expect` sha cannot distinguish a correct from an incorrect range call.
